svg.aria-label: How to write હ: one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
svg.title: Writing હ
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of હ (gujarati), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, હ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source note on variation: The teaching app animates હ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper right, circles the compact upper loop, threads through the middle turn, then continues around the broad lower bowl into its rightward finish without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the compact upper loop, middle turn, broad lower bowl, and rightward finish, but its printed form separates the upper and lower contours and makes the turns wider and more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path fits each run to the font's ink and uses a short connecting bridge between those disconnected printed contours to preserve the source's upper-loop-to-middle-turn-to-lower-bowl order and zero-lift evidence. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loop, turn, bowl, finish, and terminals differently.
svg.text: How it is written — one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
